Guardian EXCLUSIVE: Tories overstate net zero cost by nearly £500bn in apparent spreadsheet error. By Peter Walker, senior political correspondent. JSON-LD datePublished 2026-10-09T06:00:41Z (07:00 BST); dateModified 07:55:16Z (08:55 BST).
Kemi Badenoch's flagship conference policy document 'The Right Way' (100 pages, produced for the Conservative conference in Birmingham) overestimated the cost of net zero by nearly £500bn, 'seemingly after someone accidentally double-counted figures on a spreadsheet'.
THE NUMBERS: the document says 'In 2020, the Climate Change Committee (CCC) estimated that its route to net zero would cost £957bn', citing the Sixth Carbon Budget, and says gross economic costs were £1.4tn falling to £957bn after savings. 'However, the figures in the report in fact total £478bn, half of what the Tory document said.' The error 'appears to have arisen because a tally of all the costs in a CCC spreadsheet from the document also included the row showing totals for each individual column, thus doubling it.'
CCC spokesperson, on the record: 'We don't recognise this number. The committee has previously offered to meet with Ms Badenoch and talk her through our advice. That offer is, of course, still open.'
CCC's most recent analysis puts the expected cost of reaching net zero by 2050 at about £110bn, or about £4bn a year - 0.2% of GDP.
PROVENANCE OF THE ERROR: spotted by the publication Carbon Brief, which informed the Guardian. The figure appears to have been published in a report by the Institute of Economic Affairs and included in an article in the Spectator; the Conservatives may have copied it without checking.
IRONY LINE: in a foreword Badenoch notes that 'as an engineer' she is used to correctly diagnosing issues so they can be addressed; a later part of the report says 'To fix a problem we must first have an accurate understanding of what is causing it.'
Context: justifies the Conservatives' decision to scrap the 2050 net zero target introduced under Theresa May. The document is modelled in part on The Right Approach (Thatcher's Tory party, 1976).
The Conservatives and Badenoch's office were contacted for comment - no response in the piece. SINGLE-SOURCED: Guardian exclusive, not yet matched elsewhere, but the CCC quote and Carbon Brief attribution are on the record.
